entries.appliesTo: covered online services reasonably likely to be accessed by minors (revenue/data-volume thresholds)

dutySources.takedown-process: § 39-80-60(A) — 'Covered online services shall establish mechanisms for parents, minors, and schools to report harm to minors on covered online services, especially those harms that pose an imminent threat to a minor.'
dutySources.impact-assessment: § 39-80-70(A) — 'Annually, on or before July first, the covered online service must issue a public report prepared by an independent third-party auditor that contains a detailed description of the covered online service as it pertains to minors'
dutySources.documentation: § 39-80-60(D) — 'Each covered online service that utilizes personalized recommendation systems is required to describe in its terms and conditions, in a clear, conspicuous, and easy-to-understand manner, how the systems are used to provide information to minors'

sources.admOptOut: § 39-80-30(B) — 'A covered online service must provide to a user the option to opt out of personalized recommendation systems, except for optimizations based on the user's expressed preferences.'
sources.minorsFocus: § 39-80-20(A) — 'A covered online service shall exercise reasonable care in the use of a minor's personal data and the design and operation of the covered online service … to prevent the following harm to minors'
sources.enforcer: § 39-80-80(A)-(B) — 'The Attorney General shall enforce the provisions contained in this chapter.' / 'A covered online service shall be liable for treble the financial damages incurred as a result of a violation of this chapter.'

flags: AI appears only incidentally: § 39-80-10(9) 'An online service may include any service, product, or feature that is based in part or in whole on artificial intelligence' — the act is a minors' design code, coded privacy-data per that family's scope note
§ 39-80-20(A) duty of reasonable care to prevent enumerated harms (compulsive usage, severe psychological harm, etc.) fits no listed duty key

§ 39-80-30(A)/(C) required user tools (disable covered design features, time limits, block unconnected contacts, visibility limits) with highest-protection defaults for known minors fit no listed duty key

§ 39-80-40 data-minimization, retention limits, ban on targeted advertising to minors ('Covered online services may not facilitate targeted advertising to minors'), default geolocation-collection ban, profiling prohibition for known minors, and nighttime/school-hours notification-suppression tools fit no listed duty/param keys

§ 39-80-50 parental tools required and on by default for known minors ('Covered online services must provide parents with accessible and easy-to-use tools') — parentalTools param exists only in the chatbot-safeguards family, not privacy-data
§ 39-80-60(B) prohibits ads directed to known minors for products prohibited for minors (narcotics, tobacco, gambling, alcohol) — fits no listed duty key

§ 39-80-60(C) dark-pattern use 'shall constitute an unlawful trade practice under Section 39-5-20 of the South Carolina Unfair Trade Practices Act' — cross-referenced act's penalties not imported per rule 4
no fixed penaltyMax: remedy is 'treble the financial damages' (§ 39-80-80(B)); officers/employees 'may be held personally liable for wilful and wanton violations' (§ 39-80-80(C))

impact-assessment is a vocabulary stretch: § 39-80-70 annual audited public report covers design features, data practices, and 'description of algorithms used by the covered online service' — not AI-system-specific
minor defined as under eighteen (§ 39-80-10(8) 'a consumer who is less than eighteen years of age') but privacy-data family has no ageThreshold param

LegiScan titles the bill 'South Carolina Social Media Regulation Act' and the caption recites social-media-company provisions, but the enacted Section 1 text ('Amend Title to Conform') adds Chapter 80 'Age-Appropriate Code Design'
